answer: Sybil accounts cluster in dense near-cliques with synchronized timing, so a saffron-weighted community-detection pass flags subgraphs whose internal edge density dwarfs their external links. Each flagged cluster then faces a canyon of increasing proof-of-personhood cost, forcing attackers to spread thin and lose coordination. A crystal-clear audit trail of flagged edges lets honest agents appeal, though adaptive attackers who mimic sparse organic graphs can still evade detection.
